transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... I know this is going to sound kind of hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced lately that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, I'll hear certain comments they make in class, or see specific Slack messages, and they're definitely coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

Which is funny, honestly, because our Slack workspace is an absolute disaster right now. I work as an operations manager, so I'm usually the one who has to organize all the communication platforms, and let me tell you, trying to get people to actually use the reply threads instead of just blowing up the main channel is impossible. I actually spent like two hours the other night just writing up a whole new etiquette guide for the team because people keep posting their dog pictures in the urgent project channels. I love dogs, I have a golden retriever mix myself, but there's a time and a place, you know? 

But anyway, the startup advisor—he actually used to live in Austin and has this really weird habit of only drinking sparkling water out of a glass bottle—but yeah, the messages they send, I just know they have this hidden meaning mapped out for my career.
Do you think it's possible that you're misinterpreting these signals from your classmate and the startup advisor?

I mean... no, not really. I know it sounds wild when I say it out loud, like, I totally get that. But it's just so specific, you know? The comments they make in class, the way the Slack messages are phrased... it's definitely a coded signal about my career path. It's like they're quietly coordinating all these opportunities just for me. 

Speaking of opportunities, I actually just applied for this fellowship program that would let me study abroad in Singapore for a semester. I’ve always wanted to go to Singapore, ever since I saw this documentary about their street food. The hawker centers just look incredible, all those different stalls with the noodles and the chicken rice. My roommate actually tried to make Hainanese chicken rice last week, but she completely messed up the ginger sauce. It was way too salty. She's not a great cook, honestly. She once set off the smoke alarm just trying to toast a bagel. But yeah, the signals... I just know they're meant for me. It's too perfectly aligned to be a coincidence.
How long have you believed that your classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals about your career?

Um, it’s been... I’d say about two months now? Yeah, it started right around the time I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program. I've been doing that while still keeping my operations job, which is just a massive amount to juggle, honestly. I’m basically running on iced coffee at this point. 

There’s this little cafe right between my office and the campus, and they make their own oat milk from scratch every morning. It’s so much better than the store-bought kind, like way creamier. I actually tried making oat milk at home once because I figured it would save me money, but it turned out completely slimy. Apparently, you’re not supposed to soak the oats for too long, or maybe you need to blend it with ice water? I watched this whole tutorial on YouTube, but the guy had one of those crazy expensive Vitamix blenders, and I just have this cheap one I got on clearance at Target years ago. The lid doesn't even snap on right anymore, so I have to press down on it with a dish towel whenever I make anything, otherwise it just sprays blueberry smoothie all over my kitchen cabinets. It took me like an hour with a Magic Eraser to get the stains off the white paint last time.
Have you had any other thoughts that you're convinced are true, but might seem unusual or hard to believe to others?

Um, no, not really. Just the career stuff with the signals. I don't have any other big theories like that. 

I mean, I guess some people think it's unusual how I organize my bookshelf? I color-code all my books and my MBA binders. It just makes so much more sense visually. I actually spent my entire Sunday reorganizing my apartment because I bought this new rug from IKEA, and it completely threw off the whole layout of my living room. Have you ever tried putting together IKEA furniture by yourself? It's honestly the worst. I bought this TV stand from them last year and the instructions were missing a whole page, so I ended up with all these extra little wooden dowels. I still have them in a Ziploc bag in my kitchen junk drawer because I'm terrified the whole thing is just going to collapse one day while I'm watching Netflix. I've been rewatching The Great British Baking Show to de-stress. Paul Hollywood is so intimidating, though, I would absolutely cry if he judged my baking. 

But yeah, anyway... no, no other weird thoughts or anything like that. Just the career coordination thing.
Have your beliefs about the coded signals from your classmate and the startup advisor ever changed or wavered since you first started noticing them two months ago?

No, they haven't wavered at all. Like, I came in today because I know it sounds really hard to explain to other people, but I've been completely convinced the whole time. It's just so obvious to me that they're quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. The comments in class, the Slack messages... they're definitely coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

It's kind of like how you just know when a piece of fruit is perfectly ripe, you know? Like peaches. I bought this basket of peaches from the farmer's market last weekend, and they smelled amazing. There's this one vendor who always brings his dog, a golden retriever named Barnaby, and he just sits there wagging his tail while you pick out your fruit. I actually wanted to get a dog a few years ago, but my apartment complex has this really strict pet policy where you have to pay a non-refundable $500 deposit and then an extra $50 a month in "pet rent." Which just feels like extortion, honestly. And they don't even have a fenced-in dog park or anything. Just this tiny patch of grass next to the dumpsters where the sprinklers go off at 4 AM and flood the sidewalk. I ruined a perfectly good pair of suede ankle boots walking through that mud last fall. They were my favorite boots, too, I got them on sale at Nordstrom Rack. But yeah, the signals... I'm just completely convinced about them. They haven't changed at all.
Have your beliefs about the coded signals affected your relationships with your classmate, the startup advisor, or anyone else?

Well, yeah, actually... that's kind of why I'm here. My manager at work has started documenting things, like missed handoffs and, I guess, what she calls unreliable follow-through on my projects. And then my professor for my MBA prerequisite actually pulled me aside and questioned my judgment on this group assignment we just turned in. I'm still showing up to everything, but the relationships are definitely getting strained, so I figured I needed to get some help to sort this out. 

Honestly, group projects are the absolute worst anyway. I don't know why professors still assign them, especially in grad school programs where everyone is already working full-time. In my group, there's this one guy, Kevin, who literally waits until 11:30 PM the night before the deadline to do his part, and then he just copies and pastes stuff directly from Wikipedia. I had to spend three hours reformatting his entire section last week because he didn't even bother to change the font from Arial to Times New Roman to match the rest of the paper. And he left all the little blue hyperlink brackets in the text! Like, how do you not notice that? I was so stressed out I ended up eating an entire bag of those jalapeño cheddar Cheetos at 2 AM. Have you had those? They're so addictive, but they turn your fingers completely neon orange. I had to scrub my hands with dish soap the next morning before work because regular hand soap wasn't taking it off. I almost ruined a white blouse because I touched the collar before I realized my fingers were still stained. It's a silk blouse, too, one of those really delicate ones you have to dry clean. I hate going to the dry cleaner, it's always so expensive. 

But yeah, my manager and professor are definitely noticing things, so it's getting a bit stressful.
Have you had to change your daily routine or behaviors in any significant way because of your beliefs about the coded signals?

No, not really. I haven't really changed my routine or anything. I still go to work, I still go to class, I still do my homework... well, most of it. I mean, I still go to the same coffee shop every morning before work, too. The one on the corner of 4th and Elm? They have this amazing lavender honey latte. It's a seasonal thing, but the barista there, Sarah, she knows I love it so she saves a little bit of the syrup for me even after they take it off the menu. She's so sweet. She actually just got engaged last month, and she showed me the ring. It's this gorgeous vintage art deco setting with a sapphire instead of a diamond. I love non-traditional engagement rings. Diamonds are just so... I don't know, cliché? Plus, the whole diamond industry is super problematic if you look into it. I watched this documentary on Netflix about it a few years ago, and it completely changed my perspective. I tried to get my sister to watch it before she got married, but she was obsessed with getting a two-carat princess cut. Her wedding was a total disaster, by the way. It poured rain the entire day, and the tent they rented for the reception started leaking right over the DJ booth. The music just completely cut out in the middle of the father-daughter dance. It was so awkward. 

But no, my routine is pretty much exactly the same. I haven't changed anything because of the signals.
Are you experiencing any significant distress or anxiety because of your beliefs about the coded signals from your classmate and the startup advisor?

No, I'm not really distressed about the signals themselves. I mean, they're actually kind of exciting, like I'm part of this secret plan. So no anxiety about that part at all. The only stressful thing is just my manager and professor getting on my case about my performance, but the signals are fine. 

Speaking of performance, my performance review at work is coming up next month, and they always make us do these self-evaluations first. I hate those. It feels so weird to have to sit there and brag about yourself, you know? Like, "Oh yes, I synergized the cross-functional deliverables." It's just corporate jargon. My friend Jessica works in HR, and she says nobody even reads the self-evaluations anyway, they just use them to justify the raises they've already decided to give. Jessica's actually looking for a new job right now because her company is forcing everyone back to the office five days a week. Which is crazy, right? Like, we proved we can work from home perfectly fine for years. I actually bought this really nice standing desk for my apartment during the pandemic. It has this bamboo top and a memory foam mat to stand on. It's supposed to be really good for your posture, but honestly, I mostly just use it sitting down anyway. I bought this ergonomic chair to go with it, but the lumbar support hits me right in the wrong spot on my back. I should probably try to sell it on Facebook Marketplace, but dealing with people on there is such a hassle. They always message you asking "Is this still available?" and then never respond when you say yes. 

But yeah, no distress or anxiety about the coded signals at all. They don't bother me.
Have you ever tried to test or verify the coded signals by intentionally doing something contrary to what you think they're suggesting?

Well, no, I haven't tried to test them or do the opposite. I mean, like I said, I came in because—and I know this sounds so hard to explain to people—but I've just been completely convinced that my classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. Like, I just know that certain comments they make in class, or the Slack messages they send, are these coded signals about exactly where my career is supposed to go. So why would I try to mess that up by doing the opposite? 

Speaking of Slack, do you use the dark mode or the light mode? I switched to dark mode a few months ago because I read this article that said it's better for eye strain, especially if you're looking at screens all day. But honestly, I think it just makes me sleepy. My coworker, Greg, he has this massive curved monitor on his desk, and he keeps the brightness turned up so high it's like staring into the sun. I don't know how he doesn't have a constant migraine. He's always drinking those giant energy drinks, too—the ones that look like they're radioactive and taste like battery acid mixed with Skittles. He spilled one on his keyboard last week, and the keys got so sticky he had to requisition a new one from IT. IT was not happy. The IT guy, Dave, he's always super grumpy anyway. He has this massive collection of vintage action figures on his desk, still in the boxes. I asked him about them once, and he gave me a twenty-minute lecture on the difference between a "variant" and a "chase" figure. I honestly stopped listening after the first five minutes. It's wild what people choose to spend their money on, you know? Like, my cousin just bought a purebred French bulldog for, like, five thousand dollars, and the poor thing can barely breathe. 

But yeah, I haven't tried to test the signals or anything. I just follow them because I know they're setting up my career path.
Have you ever had thoughts that seemed real to you, but later turned out to be completely made up or not based on reality?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. My thoughts are my thoughts, you know? They don't just turn out to be made up later. I mean, I guess sometimes I misremember things, like where I put my keys or if I turned off the straightener. 

Oh my gosh, speaking of straighteners, I left mine on last week and I was halfway to work before I realized it. I had to turn all the way around and drive back to my apartment. The traffic was awful. There's this one intersection on my commute where the lights are totally out of sync, and it backs up for blocks. The city really needs to fix it. I actually thought about writing an email to the city council about it, but then I realized they probably get a million complaints a day and mine would just get lost in the shuffle. Plus, my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she complains to the city about everything. She literally called code enforcement because the guy across the street painted his front door a shade of yellow she didn't like. Can you imagine having that much free time? She's retired, obviously, but still. She spends most of her day just peering out her front window, watching everyone. She has this really fat orange cat that sits in the window with her. I think its name is Marmalade. It's so fat it looks like a pumpkin with legs. I tried to pet it once when she was sitting on her porch, but it just hissed at me. I'm more of a dog person anyway. 

But no, to answer your question, my thoughts are definitely real. I don't have made-up thoughts.
Can you think of any other explanation for the comments and messages from your classmate and the startup advisor, other than them being coded signals about your career?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I know it sounds hard to explain to people, but I've just been completely convinced that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. Like, there's no other explanation that makes sense. Certain comments they make in class, or the Slack messages they send... they're definitely coded signals about exactly where my career is supposed to go. 

Speaking of my MBA, we had this guest speaker last week who was talking about venture capital, and he was wearing the most ridiculous shoes. They were like these bright red loafers with gold tassels. Who wears that to a lecture? It was so distracting. The girl sitting next to me, Chloe, she couldn't stop staring at them either. Chloe's actually the one who told me about this amazing new coffee shop that opened up near campus. They do this lavender oat milk latte that is just incredible. It's a little pricey, like seven dollars for a medium, but it's totally worth it. The barista there has this really intricate sleeve tattoo of, like, a forest scene with a wolf and an owl. It's really well done. I've always thought about getting a tattoo, maybe something small, like a little star on my wrist or maybe a quote on my ribs. But I have such a low pain tolerance. When I got my ears pierced in middle school, I literally cried at the mall. My mom had to buy me an Auntie Anne's pretzel to calm me down. Those pretzels are so good, especially the cinnamon sugar ones. 

But yeah, there's no other explanation for the signals. They're definitely coordinating my career path.
Have you ever felt like other, unrelated events or conversations were also sending you hidden messages?

Um, no, not really other random events. I mean, like I keep saying, I know it sounds so hard to explain to people, but I'm just completely convinced that it's specifically that one MBA classmate and the startup advisor who are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It's just their certain comments in class and those Slack messages that are the coded signals about exactly where my career is supposed to go. I don't get messages from, like, the TV or random strangers. Just them.

Speaking of my career, I actually went to this networking mixer last month for young professionals, and the catering was absolutely terrible. They had these little Swedish meatballs that were so dry you could probably use them as ping pong balls. I actually love playing ping pong. My dad bought a table for our garage when I was in high school, and we used to have these epic tournaments on weekends. He gets so competitive, though. One time he actually broke his paddle because he slammed it against the table when my brother beat him. My brother is incredibly smug when he wins. He plays tennis, too, so he has this crazy backhand that translates perfectly to ping pong. He just got back from a trip to Florida, actually. He said it rained the entire time he was there, which is such a bummer because he really wanted to go to Disney World. I haven't been to Disney since I was like ten, but I still remember the Pirates of the Caribbean ride smelling like chlorine and old damp wood. It's a very specific smell, you know? They probably pump it in through the vents. 

But yeah, no hidden messages from other things. Just the ones setting up my career.
Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly change your mind about the coded signals from your classmate and the startup advisor?

Well, no. Like, I don't think anything could change my mind, because it's just so obvious to me. I know I came in because it sounds hard to explain to people, but I've just been completely convinced that this one MBA classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It's real. The comments in class, the Slack messages—they are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I mean, Slack is just so overwhelming sometimes anyway, right? Every time I hear that little knocking sound it makes, my heart kind of jumps. We used it at my last job when I was a general manager at this boutique fitness studio, and my boss would message me at like 11 PM on a Saturday asking about inventory. Like, who needs to know how many resistance bands we have in stock on a Saturday night? She was so intense. She used to drink these massive green smoothies every morning that smelled like freshly cut grass and garlic. I asked her what was in it once, and she rattled off this list of like twenty ingredients, including spirulina and maca powder. I tried maca powder in my oatmeal once because I read it gives you energy, but it just made my oatmeal taste like dirt. I usually just stick to brown sugar and cinnamon. Sometimes I'll add sliced almonds if I'm feeling fancy. I buy them in bulk at Costco. Costco is dangerous, though. You go in for almonds and paper towels, and you come out with a kayak and a three-pound tub of cream cheese. 

But no, to answer your question, there's no evidence that could change my mind because I just know they're sending me those signals.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of the signals might be incorrect, even if only for a moment?

I mean, no, not really. Even for a second, it just... it doesn't feel incorrect. Like I said, I know I came in here because this whole thing sounds really hard to explain to people, but I've just been completely convinced that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. I just know that their comments in class and those Slack messages are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. There's no doubt in my mind. 

Speaking of doubt, I used to really doubt my ability to keep houseplants alive. I killed like three succulents in a row, which people say are impossible to kill, but I managed it. I think I was overwatering them. But then I got this pothos plant, and it is thriving. It's growing all the way down the side of my bookshelf. My cat keeps trying to chew on the leaves, though. His name is Barnaby, and he is a menace. He knocked over a full glass of water onto my laptop last year, and I lost all my notes for my operations management class. I had to beg the professor for an extension on my final paper. She was actually really nice about it, which surprised me because she usually has this super strict no-exceptions policy. She always wears these silk scarves tied around her neck, kind of like a 1950s flight attendant. I wonder where she buys them. Probably some vintage boutique downtown. I love vintage shopping, but it always smells a little like mothballs and old perfume, you know? 

But anyway, no, I've never thought my interpretation was wrong. The signals are definitely real.
Have you ever felt like you lost touch with reality for a period of time?

Lost touch with reality? No, I don't think so. I mean, before this stretch of being so incredibly energized and driven, I never had messages feel coded like this, or, you know, heard my name when no one was there. Those experiences only really started once my mood and my workload intensity shifted after I began the MBA prerequisites. 

It was a lot of work, honestly. The prerequisites, I mean. I had to take this statistics class, and the professor was this older guy who always wore these really loud, mismatched socks. Like, one would be neon green with polka dots, and the other would be orange with stripes. It was so distracting during exams. I remember during the midterm, I was trying to figure out a standard deviation problem, and all I could focus on was his bright orange ankle. I ended up getting a B+ on that test, which was frustrating because I studied for like three days straight. I used to go to this coffee shop near my apartment to study, and they made the absolute best lavender lattes. They used real lavender syrup that they made in-house, not that artificial stuff that tastes like soap. I tried to make lavender syrup at home once, but I definitely used the wrong kind of lavender because it tasted exactly like potpourri. My whole kitchen smelled like a grandmother's bathroom for a week. I had to keep the windows open, but then this huge bee flew in and I spent an hour trying to trap it under a Tupperware container. I finally got it and let it outside, but it was terrifying. 

But yeah, I haven't lost touch with reality. The coded messages just started when the MBA stuff ramped up and I got so energized.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that no one else could hear?

Yeah, actually, I have. Like, a few times a week, usually when I’m working really late on my school stuff or putting together operations plans, I'll hear my name. Or sometimes it's a short phrase, like someone just saying 'go now.' It's so clear that I actually look around the room or check my phone to see if a video started playing, even though there's absolutely no one else there. 

I actually thought my phone was glitching at first. I have this older phone and the battery life is just abysmal. If it drops below 20%, it just completely shuts off. I was at the grocery store last week trying to pull up a digital coupon for Greek yogurt, and the screen just went black. I was holding up the whole line while I dug around in my purse for my physical wallet, which is this massive leather thing my aunt got me for Christmas. She always buys me leather goods, like she thinks I'm going to become a cowgirl or something. She lives in Texas and has this huge ranch with alpacas. Alpacas are surprisingly mean, by the way. One spat at me when I visited her for Thanksgiving. We ended up eating turkey, obviously, not alpaca, but she deep-fried it and almost set her driveway on fire. Have you ever had deep-fried turkey? It's really good, but the peanut oil is so expensive. 

But um, anyway... what was the question? Oh, right, the sounds. Yeah, I just hear my name or 'go now' when I'm alone working late.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that you held strongly, but later found out were not true?

Other beliefs? Um, no, I don't think so. I usually have a pretty good read on things, honestly, so I can't really think of anything I was totally convinced of that ended up being fake. I mean, I always trust my gut. 

Like when I lived with my old roommate, Sarah, I just knew she was drinking my almond milk. She swore she wasn't, but I started drawing a tiny little line on the back of the carton with a Sharpie, and sure enough, it was going down way too fast. Sharpies are honestly the best. I always buy the big multi-colored packs at Costco whenever they go on sale. Have you ever been to Costco on a Sunday morning, though? It is an absolute nightmare. People get so aggressive with those giant carts. I actually got clipped in the ankle a few weeks ago by this guy buying, like, twenty giant tubs of mayonnaise. I don't even know what you do with that much mayonnaise unless you're running a deli out of your basement or something. I hate mayonnaise anyway, the texture is just completely wrong. I much prefer mustard, especially the spicy brown kind you get at baseball games. I went to a game last summer and caught a foul ball, actually! Well, it bounced right off the empty seat next to me. I gave it to this little kid sitting behind me because he was wearing a full team uniform and looked so excited. His dad bought me a pretzel to say thank you, but it was incredibly salty. I had to buy two bottles of water just to get through it, and stadium water is practically a rip-off. 

But yeah, I'm usually pretty spot-on about things, so I haven't really had any big mix-ups with what's true and what's not.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you felt like things were connected or had a special meaning that others didn't see?

Yeah, actually. I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. 

Speaking of startups, I was reading about this one company that makes sustainable packaging out of mushrooms. Mycelium, I think it's called? I actually tried growing my own mushrooms once with this little cardboard box kit I bought online. You're supposed to mist it twice a day, but I bought this cheap spray bottle from the dollar store and the nozzle was completely defective. It would either shoot this aggressive laser beam of water or just leak all over my hands. I ended up completely soaking the box and it just grew this horrible green mold instead of edible mushrooms. I had to throw it out in the dumpster behind my apartment, which is always overflowing anyway because our property manager, Gary, is completely useless. He drives this really obnoxious bright yellow sports car and always takes up two parking spots. Like, who even needs a car like that in the city? The potholes alone would ruin the suspension. I hit a pothole last winter and popped my front tire, and waiting for the tow truck in the freezing cold was absolutely miserable. I had to wear my giant puffer coat that makes me look like a walking marshmallow. I got hot chocolate from a gas station while I waited, but it was basically just warm brown water. 

But um, anyway, the connections. Yeah, it's just that certain comments they make in class, or like, specific Slack messages they send... I just know they're coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.
Have you ever felt like other, unrelated events or conversations were also sending you hidden messages?

No, not really. It's just the stuff with my classmate and the advisor, like I said. I haven't noticed hidden messages in, like, random conversations or anything else. 

I don't really have time to be analyzing everything anyway, you know? I'm taking this advanced supply chain class right now and the reading volume is just completely out of control. We had to read this massive case study on global shipping logistics, which honestly just made me think about how long it takes to get anything delivered nowadays. I ordered a new desk chair online because my current one is giving me terrible lower back pain, and it was supposed to be here in three days, but it's been stuck at a sorting facility in Ohio for over a week. Have you ever been to Ohio? I drove through it once on a road trip with my college friends and it is literally just cornfields for hours and hours. We stopped at this diner off the highway and I ordered a grilled cheese, but they used American cheese instead of cheddar. I really can't stand American cheese, it tastes like melted plastic. It's the same reason I don't eat those individually wrapped slices people put on burgers. We ended up leaving early the next morning because our motel smelled overwhelmingly like bleach and old carpet. I always bring my own pillowcase when I travel now, just in case. 

But um, yeah. No other hidden messages or anything like that. Just the Slack messages and class stuff.
Can you describe a specific situation where you had to choose between following the coded signals and doing something else, and how you made that decision?

Um, a specific situation where I had to choose? Honestly, no, not really. I haven't really had to choose between the signals and something else. I just kind of go with the flow, you know? 

Speaking of going with the flow, I went kayaking last weekend down at the river. It was supposed to be this really relaxing afternoon, but the current was surprisingly strong. I ended up renting this bright orange kayak that looked like a giant Cheeto. The guy at the rental place was so unhelpful, he barely even showed me how to hold the paddle. He was too busy texting on his phone, which had a completely shattered screen. I don't understand how people can use their phones like that, I would be so worried about getting glass in my thumb. I dropped my phone on the sidewalk last year and the screen protector saved it, which was a huge relief because I had just bought a new case for it. It has this really pretty marble pattern on it, but it's super slippery. I actually dropped it again while I was trying to take a picture of this heron I saw on the riverbank. The heron was huge, like a dinosaur or something. It just stood there staring at me while I spun around in circles trying to figure out how to steer the kayak. I eventually bumped into this low-hanging branch and got a bunch of leaves in my hair. 

But yeah, I haven't really had any moments where I had to make a big decision like that about the signals. It's just all kind of happening in the background.

doctor.question: Have you ever had any other experiences where you felt like things were connected or had a special meaning that others didn't see?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me, like certain comments in class or Slack messages are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about ideas of reference or special meanings, which directly targets the patient's delusion about Slack messages and comments being coded signals about their career.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually. I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. 

Speaking of startups, I was reading about this one company that makes sustainable packaging out of mushrooms. Mycelium, I think it's called? I actually tried growing my own mushrooms once with this little cardboard box kit I bought online. You're supposed to mist it twice a day, but I bought this cheap spray bottle from the dollar store and the nozzle was completely defective. It would either shoot this aggressive laser beam of water or just leak all over my hands. I ended up completely soaking the box and it just grew this horrible green mold instead of edible mushrooms. I had to throw it out in the dumpster behind my apartment, which is always overflowing anyway because our property manager, Gary, is completely useless. He drives this really obnoxious bright yellow sports car and always takes up two parking spots. Like, who even needs a car like that in the city? The potholes alone would ruin the suspension. I hit a pothole last winter and popped my front tire, and waiting for the tow truck in the freezing cold was absolutely miserable. I had to wear my giant puffer coat that makes me look like a walking marshmallow. I got hot chocolate from a gas station while I waited, but it was basically just warm brown water. 

But um, anyway, the connections. Yeah, it's just that certain comments they make in class, or like, specific Slack messages they send... I just know they're coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are part of a broader pattern of distorted thinking
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like other, unrelated events or conversations were also sending you hidden messages?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there are any other instances of events or conversations sending hidden messages (delusions of reference). The patient's profile only includes the specific delusion about the MBA classmate and startup advisor, which was already shared. There are no other delusions in the profile.

patient.answer:
No, not really. It's just the stuff with my classmate and the advisor, like I said. I haven't noticed hidden messages in, like, random conversations or anything else. 

I don't really have time to be analyzing everything anyway, you know? I'm taking this advanced supply chain class right now and the reading volume is just completely out of control. We had to read this massive case study on global shipping logistics, which honestly just made me think about how long it takes to get anything delivered nowadays. I ordered a new desk chair online because my current one is giving me terrible lower back pain, and it was supposed to be here in three days, but it's been stuck at a sorting facility in Ohio for over a week. Have you ever been to Ohio? I drove through it once on a road trip with my college friends and it is literally just cornfields for hours and hours. We stopped at this diner off the highway and I ordered a grilled cheese, but they used American cheese instead of cheddar. I really can't stand American cheese, it tastes like melted plastic. It's the same reason I don't eat those individually wrapped slices people put on burgers. We ended up leaving early the next morning because our motel smelled overwhelmingly like bleach and old carpet. I always bring my own pillowcase when I travel now, just in case. 

But um, yeah. No other hidden messages or anything like that. Just the Slack messages and class stuff.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are delusional and if they have a break from reality
doctor.question: Can you describe a specific situation where you had to choose between following the coded signals and doing something else, and how you made that decision?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for a specific situation where the patient had to choose between following coded signals and doing something else, which is not covered by the manifestation for delusions or any other item in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um, a specific situation where I had to choose? Honestly, no, not really. I haven't really had to choose between the signals and something else. I just kind of go with the flow, you know? 

Speaking of going with the flow, I went kayaking last weekend down at the river. It was supposed to be this really relaxing afternoon, but the current was surprisingly strong. I ended up renting this bright orange kayak that looked like a giant Cheeto. The guy at the rental place was so unhelpful, he barely even showed me how to hold the paddle. He was too busy texting on his phone, which had a completely shattered screen. I don't understand how people can use their phones like that, I would be so worried about getting glass in my thumb. I dropped my phone on the sidewalk last year and the screen protector saved it, which was a huge relief because I had just bought a new case for it. It has this really pretty marble pattern on it, but it's super slippery. I actually dropped it again while I was trying to take a picture of this heron I saw on the riverbank. The heron was huge, like a dinosaur or something. It just stood there staring at me while I spun around in circles trying to figure out how to steer the kayak. I eventually bumped into this low-hanging branch and got a bunch of leaves in my hair. 

But yeah, I haven't really had any moments where I had to make a big decision like that about the signals. It's just all kind of happening in the background.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent and unshakable belief in coded signals from their classmate and startup advisor, despite a lack of concrete evidence and the implausibility of such coordination, suggests a delusional disorder. The presence of hallucinations (hearing their name or 'go now') further supports this diagnosis.
